seoTitle: Video Compressor: Shrink a File by Bitrate and Resolution
metaDescription: Make a video smaller for email or chat by lowering bitrate and resolution. See a size estimate first. Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Lowers the resolution and bitrate of a video so the file is small enough to send. You see an estimated size before you start and the real size after.
why:
File size is bitrate times duration. This tool lets you set both ends: a target height and a video bitrate in kbit/s, and it shows the arithmetic as an estimate for a one minute clip. That makes it easy to reach a limit such as 25 MB for email.

Nothing is uploaded. The file is decoded by your browser and re-encoded, so quality drops a little and the result is WebM (or MP4 where your browser can record it). It records in real time, so a 60 second clip takes about a minute and the tab must stay visible. If the result is bigger than the source, the source was already well compressed, so lower the bitrate or the height more.
howTo: Pick an output height and a bitrate. 720p at 1200 kbit/s is a common starting point.
Press Process and keep the tab visible.
Check the size shown, then download. Repeat with lower numbers if needed.

faq.q: How do I hit a size limit?
faq.a: Size in MB is about (video kbit/s + audio kbit/s) x seconds / 8 / 1024. Solve for the bitrate you can afford.

faq.q: Why is my output larger than the original?
faq.a: Browser encoders are less efficient than the encoder that made your file. Lower the bitrate or the height.

faq.q: Can I remove the audio to save space?
faq.a: Yes, untick Keep audio. Audio is small, about 64 kbit/s here.
It is a target for the browser encoder. Real files vary around it.
